claims.text: Differential atomic mobility governs premelting in Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Differential atomic mobility produces localized chemical segregation, particularly at the nanoparticle surface.
Localized surface segregation lowers the free-energy barrier for the phase transition.
The starting Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles are initially solid, compositionally homogeneous solid solutions.
Heating-rate-dependent behavior can be tested by comparing in situ TEM or synchrotron-XRD thermal cycles and complementary molecular-dynamics simulations.
Room temperature is approximately 300 °C.
The bulk melting point relevant to the proposed Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu heating ramp is approximately 1400 °C.
Premelting involves development of a liquid-like surface layer.
Atomic-size and bond-strength mismatches in the HEA promote differential atomic mobility.
Slower heating enhances atomic diffusion relative to faster heating.
Enhanced diffusion during slow heating triggers localized surface segregation.
Intrinsic configurational entropy accentuates surface melting in these HEA nanoparticles.
Slowly heated HEA nanoparticles will exhibit an earlier onset of premelting than faster-heated HEA nanoparticles.
Slowly heated HEA nanoparticles will exhibit a broadened melting transition relative to faster-heated HEA nanoparticles.
Monometallic nanoparticles will exhibit a sharper, higher-temperature melting transition than the HEA nanoparticles.
The HEA nanoparticles have a distinct surface-melting temperature below their bulk melting temperature.
The premelted surface-layer thickness is sensitive to heating rate.
The hypothesis applies within a heating-rate regime in which atomic diffusion is the dominant kinetic process and may fail when heating is too rapid for diffusion.
Substrate-induced stresses can overshadow the intrinsic effects of chemical complexity.

Absence of measurable heating-rate-dependent differences in premelting onset, surface-layer formation, and segregation, or comparable behavior in monometallic controls, would falsify the proposed mechanism.
